column1: # lib/md-targets.sh: which .md files did this tool call write?
#   expect   `|` separated paths relative to the fixture root, or `-` for none
#   tool     the tool_name put in the JSON
#   cwd      directory put in the JSON, relative to the fixture root (`.` = root)
#   env      one NAME=VALUE exported for this case, or `-` for none
#   payload  tool_input.command for Bash, tool_input.file_path otherwise
# Fields are separated by a single TAB and a run of tabs collapses into one, so
# `-` is used instead of an empty field. In the payload, \n becomes a newline,
# \t a tab and @FX@ the absolute fixture root.
# Every case also carries a tool_response mentioning .md files, which must never
# become a target: only tool_input is allowed to decide.
# --- only a redirection whose target ends in .md marks a write ---
# Every `>` of the segment is scanned, so one inside a quoted string cannot
# hide the real one. The source of `cat a.md > out.md` is still collected.
# --- cp / mv report the destination only ---
# --- the `&` of `\&`, `>&`, `&>` and `2>&1` is not a segment boundary ---
# --- `>|` is a clobbering redirection, never a pipe ---
# --- a segment led by git is never a target, even when it redirects ---
# --- cd is tracked, so a relative path resolves against its own segment ---
# --- mtime: a file this call cannot have written is dropped ---

column5: echo a > d.md && echo b >> ./d.md && echo c > "$(pwd)/d.md"
